tools.name: get_protocol_info
tools.description: Returns the SAAX Protocol version, available capability count, and the URL to the specification. Call this when an agent needs a one-time overview of the protocol. For pricing, use get_routing_fee. For the full capability list, use list_capabilities. For a liveness check, use ping.

tools.name: get_routing_fee
tools.description: Returns the current routing fee schedule. Call this before initiating a routing request to determine the expected cost. For capability discovery, use list_capabilities. For protocol overview, use get_protocol_info.

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Returns a lightweight liveness response. Call this to verify the endpoint is reachable. Do not use for discovery, capability listing, or pricing — use get_protocol_info, list_capabilities, or get_routing_fee instead.

tools.name: route_request
tools.description: Submits a capability request and returns ranked supplier matches. Commitment creation with payment runs through the HTTP POST /route endpoint, not this tool. Use list_capabilities first to discover available capabilities. For commitment lookup after routing, use get_commitment.

tools.name: get_commitment
tools.description: Returns the full commitment object for a given commitment ID — including terms, state, manifest hash, and evidence references. Call this when an agent needs the complete commitment record. For status-only polling, use get_commitment_status. For listing all commitments for a subscriber, use list_comm

tools.name: list_capabilities
tools.description: Returns the capabilities currently indexed by the SAAX Router, with supplier counts per capability. Call this to discover what can be routed. For pricing of a specific capability, use get_routing_fee. For protocol overview, use get_protocol_info.

tools.name: list_commitments
tools.description: Returns all commitments associated with a subscription email. Requires an active SAAX Premium subscription. Call this to retrieve commitment history for a subscriber. For a single commitment by ID, use get_commitment. For status-only checks, use get_commitment_status.

tools.name: get_commitment_status
tools.description: Returns only the current lifecycle state for a given commitment ID, plus the recommended next action for the calling agent. Call this before retrying any commitment that timed out — an unknown outcome is a status check, not another POST. The next_action field tells the agent whether to retry, poll,

tools.name: create_commitment
tools.description: Creates a governed commitment between a buyer and a seller and persists it to the SAAX commitment store. The commitment is settlement-rail-neutral: settlementRail is metadata only (x402, mpp, ap2, acp, or unspecified) and is NEVER a prerequisite. Returns the new commitment id (saax_<hash>), createdA

tools.name: get_evidence_verification
tools.description: Verifies external evidence against a commitment's acceptance criteria. Requires an active SAAX Premium subscription. For authority proof validation, use get_authority_validation.

tools.name: get_authority_validation
tools.description: Validates an authority proof against a commitment. Requires an active SAAX Premium subscription. For evidence verification, use get_evidence_verification.

tools.name: get_commitment_history
tools.description: Returns the append-only lifecycle event ledger for a commitment � every recorded transition with actor, authority reference, state version, and evidence reference. The caller must present an EIP-712 authority proof binding its identity to the commitment. Read-only; reconciles the authoritative commi

tools.name: get_recovery_status
tools.description: Returns the authoritative commitment state, the caller's authorization status (active/revoked/expired), whether the commitment is recoverable, and the caller's permitted next actions. Reconciles the durable commitment row and the caller's authorization record before returning. The caller must presen

tools.name: get_pending_actions
tools.description: Returns the lifecycle actions the caller (verified by EIP-712 proof) may currently perform on a commitment � derived from the canonical transition map, the caller's role, and the caller's durable authorization scope. Read-only. For full recovery context, use get_recovery_status.

tools.name: resume_commitment
tools.description: Lets an independently authorized replacement agent continue a commitment. Reconciles the authoritative state, verifies the caller's EIP-712 authority proof, and executes the requested nonfinancial transition through the canonical transition engine. The replacement agent must hold its OWN durable aut

tools.name: cancel_commitment
tools.description: Cancels a commitment when the caller (verified by EIP-712 proof) holds buyer or authority authorization with cancel scope. Terminal and nonfinancial � no payment, refund, or settlement is executed. Reconciles authoritative state first. Idempotent via idempotencyRef.

tools.name: close_commitment
tools.description: Closes a fulfilled commitment (settled -> finalized) when the caller (verified by EIP-712 proof) holds system or authority authorization. Nonfinancial � no settlement, escrow release, or refund is executed. Reconciles authoritative state first. Idempotent via idempotencyRef.

tools.name: prepare_commitment
tools.description: Prepares a free, NONBINDING signed proposal (preflight) for a desired SAAX capability. Validates capability, schema/version/digest, units, and the exact supported network/asset/rail/mode combination; returns a provider-signed proposal binding the request digest and normalized terms. Creates NO agree

tools.name: accept_commitment
tools.description: Accepts a signed preflight proposal with explicit buyer authorization and creates exactly ONE authenticated SAAX commitment. Revalidates the proposal (trusted provider key, profile version, expiry, combination, manifest digest), verifies the BUYER'S SIGNATURE over the exact proposal digest and terms

tools.name: submit_evidence
tools.description: Durably submits evidence for a commitment. The caller must present an EIP-712 authority proof; the recovered signer must hold an unrevoked, unexpired provider or buyer authorization on the commitment (verified in-transaction against the durable registry). tools.name: list_evidence
tools.description: Returns the durable evidence records for a commitment (stable identifiers, integrity references, submitter attribution, status, timestamps � never raw payload content). The caller must present an EIP-712 authority proof and hold an active authorization on the commitment. Commitment-scoped: callers w

tools.name: verify_evidence
tools.description: Sets the verification status of a submitted evidence record to verified or rejected. The caller must present an EIP-712 authority proof and hold an unrevoked, unexpired EVALUATOR authorization on the commitment (verified in-transaction). Idempotent per verdict: re-verifying with the same verdict rep

tools.name: raise_dispute
tools.description: Raises a durable dispute on a commitment and transitions it to the disputed state. The caller must present an EIP-712 authority proof and hold an unrevoked, unexpired authorization on the commitment (verified in-transaction). Disputes may only be raised from evidence_submitted or fulfilled states pe

tools.name: resolve_dispute
tools.description: Records an evaluator decision on an open dispute and transitions the commitment to the canonical nonfinancial outcome (continue|rework|satisfied|against). The caller must present an EIP-712 authority proof and hold an unrevoked, unexpired EVALUATOR authorization on the commitment (verified in-transa

tools.name: list_disputes
tools.description: Returns the durable dispute records for a commitment (dispute identifiers, status, resolution, attribution, timestamps). The caller must present an EIP-712 authority proof and hold an active authorization on the commitment. Commitment-scoped: callers with no authorization see nothing. Optional statu

tools.description: Returns the detailed record for one supplier in the SAAX Router index: identifier, name, description, services (name/endpoint/version), owner and source provenance. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_protocol_info, list_commitments, get_commitment_status · Private data: get_commitment, get_commitment_status, create_commitment, get_recovery_status, submit_evidence, list_evidence, verify_evidence, resolve_dispute, list_disputes, get_supplier_details · Public sink: route_request, list_commitments, get_commitment_status, submit_evidence.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_protocol_info, list_commitments, get_commitment_status · Private data: get_commitment, get_commitment_status, create_commitment, get_recovery_status, submit_evidence, list_evidence, verify_evidence, resolve_dispute, list_disputes, get_supplier_details · Public sink: route_request, list_commitments, get_commitment_status, submit_evidence

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
